output.brief: The handler change is probably not the cause, so don't send the breach notice. Since 1 September, Corvane's tags printed at Harlow Bay check-in on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time. Before the switch the rate was 1.5%. Those bags go to the manual encode desk, where waits rose from 7 to about 30 minutes. About 91% of the extra missed bags reached the lateral after it closed. Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crews, stayed flat, and so did Corvane's transfer tags. On 14–16 October, counters that used the old Brackwater stock from stores failed at only 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12.1%. The rise follows the tag stock, not the crews or the airport's readers. I can't yet say whether the stock is defective or the printer heat settings are wrong for it. Next steps: switch back to Brackwater now, since about five weeks of it are in stores. Then test Fennick with the printer settings checked. Hold off on a defect claim against Fennick until that test is done. Withdraw the breach notice and the fee withholding. Asking the airport for an extra encode desk in the evening bank is a reasonable stopgap.
